doc.title: Don Alias interviewed by Monk Rowe, New York City, New York, January 6, 2002

chapter: Jaco, Weather Report and pop work
title: Chuck Mangione and surviving on old hits
summary: Alias admires acts that survive on their hits, citing Mangione, whom he plays with.

story.theme_name: Late-career reflections: awards, legacy and life lessons
story.community_name: Critics, polls and the jazz press

blocks.x: I like that whole scene where an act or a musician can survive playing his old stuff. I like that. You know like Mangione? He’s still — what is his tune?
“Feels So Good” and all that stuff.

“Land of Make Believe.” He’s still surviving in that market, where people will come, they’re older, forties and fifties, but still remember that scene, you know, because the seventies was a great time. And they would come through and they would see Chuck and he’s still surviving off of that stuff. But surviving really good. Because he gets good musicians, and we get a chance to play.
